title: TRADE LICENSE
content:
Trade License is issued under the Taxation Rules of local government. It is issued by the local government of the respective areas. Every business entity should obtain a Trade License from each local government where it operates. Usually banks in Bangladesh will not allow a business entity to operate its bank account without a valid trade license, thus making Trade License a mandatory permit. If a business entity has more than one place of business, it must obtain Trade License from each local government.  It is issued for one year and has to be renewed annually. Trade License attracts some government fees, which usually depends on the type of business.

Below, we have described the process of obtaining Trade License for businesses that operate within the Dhaka City Corporation area. Other local governments have similar rules. You are advised to contact the respective local government for more information.

TRADE LICENSE FOR A COMMERCIAL FIRM

PROCESS STEPS:

title: STEP 1: PROCURE THE PROPER FORM FROM THE PROPER OFFICE.

For assistance with step 1: procure the proper form from the proper office. ZCA LEGAL is here to support you throughout the process.

Dhaka City Corporation (DCC) has two forms for a trade license depending on the type of business. A commercial firm must use the “K” Form. Even though the ten zonal offices use the same K Form, a business must buy the form from its respective zonal office. A seal and the initials of the officer selling the form is what distinguishes it from that of other zones. The form costs Tk. 10.

title: PATENT IN BANGLADESH
content: An application for a patent may be made by any Bangladeshi or any foreigner, and by alone or jointly with any other person. The application must be made to the  in the prescribed form. The application must contain a declaration that the applicant is in possession of an invention, whereof he, or in the case of a joint application one at least of the applicants, claims to be the true and first inventor or the legal representative or assign of such inventor and for which he desires to obtain a patent, and must be accompanied by complete specification.

title: For assistance with specifications, ZCA LEGAL is here to support you throughout the process.
content: An application must contain a complete specification or provisional specification. A provisional specification must describe the nature of the invention. A complete specification must particularly describe and ascertain the nature of the invention and the manner in which the same is to be performed. A specification, whether provisional or complete, must commence with the title, and in the case of a complete specification must end with a distinct statement, of the invention claimed. If the applicant does not leave a complete specification with his application, s/he may leave it at any subsequent time within nine months from the date of the application The Registrar may require that suitable drawings/model or sample of anything illustrating the invention shall be supplied and such drawings/model or sample shall be part of the complete specification.

title: ADVERTISEMENT ON ACCEPTANCE OF APPLICATION
content: On the acceptance of an application the Registrar shall give notice thereof to the applicant and shall advertise the acceptance and with the drawings (if any) shall be open to public inspection.

title: OPPOSITION
content: Any person at any time within four months from the date of the advertisement of the acceptance of an application give notice at the DPDT of opposition to the grant of the patent. The opponent must state the grounds of his opposition.

title: GRANT AND SEALING OF PATENT
content: If there is no opposition a patent shall be granted, subject to such conditions as the authority thinks expedient, to the applicant, or in the case of a joint application to the applicants jointly, and the Controller shall cause the Patent to be sealed with the seal of the Patent Office.

title: TERM OF PATENT
content: The term limited in every patent for the duration thereof is sixteen years from its date and renewal is required after four years up to 15 years. In case of priority, the commencement of four years shall start from the date of priority application.

title: ACCEPTANCE OR REJECTION OF TRADEMARK BY THE REGISTRAR
content: After filing the application, the Registrar may either accept or reject or order to correct or modify the application. An application for registration of a trade mark may be accepted either absolutely or subject to conditions or limitations. The Registrar, on receipt of the application, issues Official Filing Receipt. The document contains all relevant filing details on the trademark e.g. Application Number, date of application, the trademark etc.). If the Registrar reject any application, s/he should issue a show cause letter to the applicant. The applicant must submit reply to the show cause notice and may seek a hearing in the matter within three (3) months otherwise, the application will be deemed abandoned

title: JOURNAL PUBLICATION
content: After an application is accepted by the Registrar, s/he shall provide a Journal Notification to the applicant for the advertisement of the mark. Afterwards the applicant is required to deposit journal fees though pay order/treasury chalan/bank draft. Then DPDT will send the mark to Bangladesh Government Press (BG Press) for publication.

title: OPPOSITION OF THE MARK
content:
After BG Press publishes the mark, any person may within two (2) months from the date of the publication give notice of Opposition to the Registrar using prescribed form.

The Registrar shall send a copy of the Notice of Opposition to the Applicant and the Applicant shall within Two month of receipt of the Notice of Opposition, file a Counter-Statement of the grounds for which it relies for its application to be registered. Failure to file the Counter-Statement within the prescribed period will result in the application being deemed abandoned. The applicant may seek extension of time for filing Counter-Statement along with Govt. fees.

Where a Counter-Statement is filed, the Registrar shall furnish a copy thereof to the Opponent. The parties are required to file evidence by way of Affidavit and the Registrar shall, after hearing the parties, decide on whether the application should be registered or not. The Registrar’s decision shall be subject to appeal to the High Court.

title: REGISTRATION OF THE MARK
content: If there is no opposition, DPDT will inform the applicant to pay certification fees. The applicant is required to submit the money receipt of the certification fees to DPDT. On the registration of a trade mark the Registrar shall issue to the applicant a certificate in the prescribed form of the registration thereof sealed with the seal of the Trade Marks Registry.

title: TERM AND RENEWAL
content:
A registered trademark is valid for an initial period of seven (7) years from the date of filing and renewable thereafter for successive periods of Ten (10) years.

Renewal fees must be paid before the expiry date but not more than six months prior the expiry. Late renewals available, normally up to four months after expiry date, with payment of late fees. Extensions at the direction of Registrar are liberally granted with payment of additional fees.

title: ASSIGNMENT OF TRADEMARK
content: The Registered proprietor of a Trade mark has power to assign the registered trademark with or without goodwill of the business in respect of all or some of the goods for which it is registered. Where a person becomes entitled by assignment or transmission to a registered trademark, he shall make application to the Registrar (in the prescribed manner) to register his title and the Registrar shall, on receipt of the application and on proof of title to his satisfaction, register the Assignee as the proprietor of the trademark.

title: LICENSING OF TRADEMARK
content: Licenses must be recorded with the authority to be effective. Application for record must be made to the Registrar.

title: REMEDY FOR INFRINGEMENT
content: Where the rights of a proprietor of a registered trademark has infringed, s/he can initiate civil proceeding or criminal proceeding for remedy. Any suit regarding the infringement of trademark, or to establish the right or any ratified right respecting trademark shall be instituted in the Court of District Judge within whose jurisdiction the infringement occurred. A criminal proceeding has to be instituted in the Court of Metropolitan Magistrate or any other 1st class Judicial Magistrate. Remedy in a suit for infringement may be availed in the form of injunction, damages, an accounts of profit, destruction or erasure of falsifying trademark, delivery up the goods marked with false trademark.

title: BENEFITS OF TRADEMARK REGISTRATION
content:
Trademark registration offers several advantages for businesses and individuals.

Let’s explore some of the key benefits:

title: Exclusive Usage Rights:
content: Trademark registration grants exclusive rights over the trademark. Owners can legally prevent others from using a similar or identical mark for their products or services without authorization.

title: Builds Goodwill:
content: Registering a trademark helps establish goodwill and trust in a brand. .

title: Differentiates Products and Services:
content:
A trademark distinguishes goods and services from competitors, creating a unique brand identity. .

Ensures Product Quality:

Trademark registration ensures product quality. .

title: Creation of an Asset:
content: A registered trademark becomes an intellectual asset for the business. .

title: Usage of Ⓡ Symbol:
content: Registered trademarks can use the Ⓡ symbol, indicating legal protection and authenticity. .

title: Protection against Infringement:
content: Trademark registration provides legal recourse against unauthorized usage by third parties. .

title: Once registered, a trademark remains valid for ten years, renewable indefinitely. .
content:
In summary, trademark registration is essential for brand recognition, trust-building, and safeguarding your unique identity in the market.

content: Copyright may be assigned, transferred or licensed. The Copyright Office has prescribed form for transfer.

title: REMEDIES AGAINST INFRINGEMENT
content: There are three kinds of remedies against infringement of copyright, namely:

content: The owner of the copyright can bring civil action in which reliefs such as Anton Pillar Order (Search Order) injunction, accounts and damages can be sought. content: Criminal remedies provides for the imprisonment of the accused or imposition of fine or both, seizure of infringing copies etc. Criminal proceedings are available in order to punish the persons who have violated the copyright law.

title: ADMINISTRATIVE REMEDIES
content: Administrative remedies consist of moving to the Registrar of copyrights to ban the import of infringing copies into Bangladesh, when the infringement is by way of such importation and the delivery of the confiscated infringing copies to the owner of the copyright.

title: PROPRIETORSHIP
content:
This guide provides information on registration of a sole proprietorship in Bangladesh. To learn about various types of business entities in Bangladesh, refer to start a business in Bangladesh.

Sole proprietorship is the simplest form of business structure in Bangladesh. However, it is suitable only for very small single-owner type business that does not carry any risks. Unlike a private limited liability company, a sole proprietorship does not provide limited liability protection and your personal assets are not protected from business risks.

title: SOLE-PROPRIETORSHIP – KEY FACTS
content: A sole proprietorship in Bangladesh does not constitute a separate legal entity therefore it is not distinct from the owner/ proprietor. The business owner is personally accountable for all liabilities incurred during the course of the business.

title: A local commercial address must be provided as the business address for the sole proprietorship.
content: Profits of the sole proprietorship are treated as income of the individual who owns the entity, thus it is subjected to a tax rate as that of personal income.

title: As a Bangladesh sole proprietorship is not a legal entity, it cannot register another business firm.
content:
Sole proprietorships do not need to audit their accounts as any profits will be taxed as personal taxes is the basic requirement for proprietorship.

Trade License needs to be renewed annually.

title: For assistance with considerations for foreigners, ZCA LEGAL is here to support you throughout the process.
content: Practically, a sole proprietorship is not an option for foreigners. Foreign business professionals should incorporate a private limited company instead. For further details about private limited companies, refer to company registration in Bangladesh guide.

title: DOCUMENTS REQUIRED AND REGISTRATION PROCEDURE
content:
For assistance with documents required and registration procedure, ZCA LEGAL is here to support you throughout the process.

Proposed business name in Bangla

content:

Copy of National ID for the owner.

title: No profit sharing: You accrue all income generated by the business.
content:
Ease of termination: Terminating a sole proprietorship is easier, less time consuming and less expensive than other business entities.

Least compliance requirements: You are free of the obligation of filing returns annually and only need to renew your membership every year.

title: For assistance with sole proprietorship disadvantages, ZCA LEGAL is here to support you throughout the process.
content:
No separate legal entity: You are inseparable from your business. This makes you financially and legally responsible for all debts and legal actions against the business.

Unlimited liability: Creditors may sue you for debts incurred and can also obtain a court order to claim against your personal assets, including your property.

No corporate tax benefits or incentives: Taxes are determined at your personal income tax rate and you do not enjoy special tax benefits that are available to a private limited company.

Limited capital: Capital is limited to your personal finances and the profits generated by the business. Thus, business expansion is limited and difficult.

No perpetual succession: The business lives and dies with you as you and the business are one and the same thing. However, after the death of the owner of proprietorship, the successor may continue the business in the same name.

Low public perception: This entity is the least preferred for serious businesses as nobody would be willing to lend you large sums of money. It is also difficult to attract high-caliber employees, or senior level executives who usually look for a more advanced form of business structure such as a private limited company.

Sale/transfer of all or part of the business: You can transfer the business only by the sale of business assets.

title: PARTNERSHIP
content:
A partnership is a type of business structure where two or more partners start an entity to do business. For a partnership to exist, there must always be two or more partners.

A Partnership is defined by the , (the “Partnership Act”) as ‘the relation between persons who have agreed to share profits of the business carried on by all or any of them acting for all’. This definition gives three minimum requirements to constitute a partnership:

title: the object of the agreement must be to share the profits of business intended to be carried on by the partnership, and
content:
the business must be carried on by all the partners or by any of them acting for all of them. The term ‘person’ is not defined by the Partnership Act.

It is not compulsory to register your partnership firm as there are no penalties for non-registration. However, it is advisable since the following rights are denied to an unregistered firm:

A partner cannot file a suit in any court against the firm or other partners for the enforcement of any right arising from a contract or right conferred by the Partnership Act

title: A right arising from a contract cannot be enforced in any Court by or on behalf of your firm against any third party
content:
Further, the firm or any of its partners cannot claim a set off (i.e. mutual adjustment of debts owned by the disputant parties to one another) or other proceedings in a dispute with a third party.

PARTNERSHIP – QUICK FACTS

title: LIABILITY
content: A partnership is considered as a separate legal identity (i.e. separate from its owners) in Bangladesh only if the partnership is registered.

title: All the partners of a partnership are liable severally and jointly for the liability of the partnership.

title: TAXATION
content: From a tax perspective, partnerships in Bangladesh are not taxed at the entity level and profits are treated as part of each partners’ personal income and are taxed at personal income tax rates.

title: The partners can be natural persons or companies.

title: HOW TO TRANSFER SHARES OF A BANGLADESHI COMPANY
content: Shares in a company registered in Bangladesh is a movable property and transferable in a manner provided in the Articles of Association of the company. Below we have described the procedure of transferring shares of a private limited company registered in Bangladesh.

title: In a private limited company, the right to transfer shares may be restricted.
content: There is a prescribed form for share transfer known as Form 117.

title: FIRST STEP: CHECK FOR RESTRICTION IN THE ARTICLES AND/OR OTHER AGREEMENTS, LICENSES, PERMITS, APPROVALS.
content: For assistance with first step: check for restriction in the articles and/or other agreements, licenses, permits, approvals., ZCA LEGAL is here to support you throughout the process.

title: SHARE TRANSFER RESTRICTIONS IN ARTICLES OF ASSOCIATION
content:
The share transfer in a Private Limited Company can be restricted by the Articles of Association (AOA). Hence, the Articles of Association of the Company must be reviewed before beginning the share transfer procedure. It is common in Bangladesh that the company’s articles of association usually contain pre-agreed procedures set out that are required to be followed for any transfer of shares in the company.

Restrictions on right of the shareholders to transfer shares are usually in the form of pre-emption. Which means that if a shareholder wishes to sell some or all of his shares, such shares must first be offered to other existing members of the private limited company at a price determined by the Directors or the Auditor of the Company. In no existing shareholder is interested, then shares of the Company can be freely transferred to an outsider.

If there is any restriction or special procedures, those restriction or procedure must be followed for any share transfer.

title: SHARE TRANSFER RESTRICTIONS IN ANY LAWS, AGREEMENT, LICENSE, PERMIT, APPROVAL
content: All the license, permits, agreement etc. should be checked for any restriction imposed on the transfer of shares of the company. If there is any restriction, prior approval should be obtained.

title: STEP 2: NOTIFY THE COMPANY.
content: The shareholder planning to transfer the shares should serve notice in writing to the Board of Directors of the Company about intention to transfer share of the company. The Director may have the powers to refuse registration of transfer of shares under certain circumstances – prescribed in the Articles of Association. The Board of Directors should hold a board meeting and approve the transfer of the shares. The Director should also issue a certificate in this regard.

title: STEP 3: PAYMENT OF THE PRICE OF THE SHARES
content: Once the company provides its approval, the payment of the price of the shares should took place. If both the buyer and seller are local or foreigner, no proof of the payment is required. However, if the seller is a Bangladeshi and the buyer is a foreigner,  will require bank encashment letter for the share transfer.

title: STEP 4: EXECUTE THE FORM 117 AND PAYMENT OF STAMP DUTY
content:
Once the above steps are completed, the shareholder who is transferring the shares should visit Registrar of Joint Stock Companies and Firms (RJSC) and should sign the Form 117 at the presence of the officials of the RJSC. Other required documents should also be supplied to RJSC.

Stamp duty is payable on the face value of each share. Once the Form 117 is signed, a copy of the same should be delivered to the Company.

title: OBJECT CLAUSE AMENDMENT IN THE MOA
content:
An objects clause is a provision in a company’s Memorandum of Association stating the purpose and range of activities for which the company is carried on. The purpose of the object clause is to outline and limit the activities which the company is permitted to undertake. Anything which exceeds those limits is ultra vires (beyond the legal power or authority) of the company and may be void.

Below we have describe the process of amending the object clause of a company registered in Bangladesh.

content:
For assistance with step 2: application to the high court division, ZCA LEGAL is here to support you throughout the process.

An application should be prepared for filling with the designated Company bench of High Court Division of the . The application should be supported by an Affidavit. title: STEP 3: ADMISSION HEARING
content: After filling of the application, the Bench officer will assign a matter number to the application. The matter will appear in the daily cause list of the Court and in time the matter will be heard by the Court. After hearing and upon perusal of documents, the Court may admit the matter. If admitted, the court will direct to publish a legal notice in two daily newspapers in respect of the admitted matter, and to serve a notice to the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies and Firms (RJSC).

title: STEP 4: PUBLICATION OF THE LEGAL NOTICE AND AFFIDAVIT OF COMPLIANCE
content:
Pursuant to the order of the Court, legal notice should be published in the designated newspapers and copies of newspaper carrying the advertisement shall be collected.

An affidavit of compliance is required to be submitted to the court along with the copy of the legal notice published earlier on the specified newspaper in time specified by the court. Upon submission of the documents, the case would be appeared on the daily cause list of the court for hearing.

title: STEP 5: HEARING AND DONATION
content: Upon hearing, if the court thinks proper, the court may pass final order. It is customary for the court to require some donation to some charitable organization. The court may fix the donation amount and the charitable organization. After making the payment to the charitable organization and submitting compliance in this regard before the court, the final order will be supplied to the petitioner.

WINDING UP OF A COMPANY IN BANGLADESH

In Bangladesh, the winding up of a company may be either –

Voluntary; or

By the court; or

title: Voluntary winding up is usually undertaken by solvent companies, except in the case of creditor’s voluntary winding up.
content: Below we have described the process of voluntary winding up by passing a special resolution.

title: PROCEDURE FOR VOLUNTARY WINDING UP:
content:
For assistance with procedure for voluntary winding up:, ZCA LEGAL is here to support you throughout the process.

FIRST STEP: PREPARING DOCUMENTS:

title: DECLARATION OF SOLVENCY
content:
A declaration of solvency has to be prepared and signed by the directors. The declaration will contain statement of the company’s assets and liabilities as at the latest predictable date before making of the declaration. The declaration will also state that the company has no debts or that it will be able to pay its debt in full within such period not exceeding there years from the commencement of the winding up.

The declaration must be verified by an affidavit to the effect that the directors have made a full inquiry into the affairs of the company. The declaration will be signed by all the directors of the company or, in the case of a company having more than two directors, the majority of the directors.

title: ACCOUNTS AND AUDIT
content:
Profit and Loss Account and audited Balance Sheet will be prepared up to the latest predictable date as mentioned above and audited. Auditor’s report should be obtained.

SECOND STEP: BOARD MEETING AND EXTRA ORDINARY GENERAL MEETING

title: For assistance with board meeting, ZCA LEGAL is here to support you throughout the process.
content:
A Board meeting will be convened pursuant to the rules of Companies Act and Articles of the company. Majority of the directors should be present at the meeting. In the meeting, the directors will approve:

a. Audited accounts;

title: b. The declaration of the Directors;
content: The directors will also call an extra ordinary general meeting for passing the special resolution to wound up the company. After the meeting, the declaration and the affidavit (prepared in the first step) should be notarized.

title: FILLING OF THE DECLARATION WITH THE RJSC
content: The declaration should be filed with the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies and Firms within 5 weeks from the date of the declaration.

title: EXTRAORDINARY GENERAL MEETING
content: The extraordinary general meeting will be held and the special resolution will be passed. The special resolution will approve the – i) winding up; ii) appointment of the liquidator and fix the liquidator’s remuneration.

title: FILLING WITH RJSC
content:
The content of the extraordinary general meeting (along with Form VIII) and the appointment of the liquidator will be filed with the RJSC.

THIRD STEP: APPOINTMENT OF LIQUIDATOR

title: For assistance with liquidator, ZCA LEGAL is here to support you throughout the process.
content: Immediately after the special resolution is passed, the liquidator will accept the appointment and will assume office and ensure that RJSC is notified about his/her appointment. Within thirty days after liquidator is appointed, the liquidator will give notice of his appointment as such to the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes having jurisdiction to assess the company.

title: GAZETTE PUBLICATION:
content: Notice of any special resolution or extraordinary resolution for winding up a company voluntarily shall be given by the company within ten days of the passing of the same by advertisement in the official Gazette, and also in a newspaper, if any circulating in the district where the registered office of the company is situate. The appointment of the liquidator should also be mentioned in the advertisement.

title: For assistance with agm (if required), ZCA LEGAL is here to support you throughout the process.
content:
In the event of the winding up continuing for more than one year, the liquidator shall arrange an Annual General Meeting of the company at the end of the first year from the commencement of the winding up and of each succeeding year, or as soon thereafter as may be convenient within ninety days, of the close of the year, and shall lay before the meeting an account of his acts and dealings and of the conduct of the winding up during the proceeding year and a statement in the prescribed form containing the prescribed particulars with respect to the position of the liquidation.

FORTH STEP: FINAL MEETING AND FILLING WITH THE RJSC

title: For assistance with final account, ZCA LEGAL is here to support you throughout the process.
content: The liquidator will prepare a final account of the winding up showing how the winding up has been conducted and the assets of the company has been disposed of. Then s/he will call an extra ordinary general meeting.

title: For assistance with extra ordinary general meeting, ZCA LEGAL is here to support you throughout the process.
content:
Notice of the meeting will be given by advertisement specifying the time, place and object of the meeting not less than one month before the meeting in the official gazette and also in a newspaper circulating in the district where the registered office of the company is situated.

In the extra ordinary general meeting, a special resolution will be passed relating to the disposal of the books and papers of the company.

title: FILLING
content: A return of the winding up meeting will be filed with the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies and Firms within one week of the meeting. After holding of the final meeting and the submission of the documents to the Registrar, the legal entity of the company will be dissolved.

title: LIAISON OR BRANCH OFFICE IN BANGLADESH
content:
Branch or Liaison Office is one of the two options for foreign investors wishing to setup their presence in Bangladesh. The other option is incorporating a Bangladeshi subsidiary company. The information presented below provides details of setting up a Branch or Liaison office in Bangladesh.

Approval of  is the primary requirement for setting up a Branch or Liaison office in Bangladesh

title: A Liaison/Representative Office of a foreign Company can perform very limited activities, which includes:
content:
maintain liaison/ coordination between principal and local agents, distributors/exporters’ institutions through correspondences, personal contracts and other electronic media.

collect, compile analyze and disseminate business information related to its field of activities as mentioned in the approval letter.

A Liaison/Representative office will have no local source of income in Bangladesh. All setup and operational costs including salaries of the expatriates and local employees of the Liaison or Representative office will have to borne by the parent company aboard

No outward remittances of any kind from Bangladesh sources will be allowed except the amount brought in from abroad (the unspent part).

title: A Branch office of a foreign company can engage in commercial activities with prior approval of BIDA.
content: A Branch office may have local source of income from the approved field of business activities in Bangladesh and with the prior approval of BIDA.

title: KEY FACTS ABOUT BOTH BRANCH AND LIAISON OFFICE IN BANGLADESH
content:
The activities of a Branch and Liaison office shall remain confined to the areas and for the period of time mentioned and approved in approval letter issued by BIDA. If the company intends to continue their Office beyond the period approval, they will have to apply for necessary renewal/ extension in the prescribed form with proper documents at least 2 (two) months before the expiry of the current term.

If the approved company intends to employ any foreign nationals(s) in their Office, work permits should be obtained from the BIDA.

An amount of foreign exchange equivalent to the sum of not less than US$ 50,000 or equivalent as estimated initial establishment cost and 6(six) months operational expenses of the Office must be brought in as inward remittance in Bangladesh within 02(two) months from the date of issuance of the BIDA permission letter. For this purpose, the Office shall have to open an account with any scheduled bank of Bangladesh as per the instructions contained in the Guidelines for Foreign Exchange transactions for receipt of remittances.

Quarterly return of incomes and expenditures out of remittances received from abroad shall have to be submitted to the BIDA, concerned Bank, National Board of Revenue and Bangladesh Bank with documentary evidences.

Any change(s) of present address shall be intimated to the BIDA for necessary action and approval before the proposed change is carried out.

The permitted Office shall have to obtain clearances/ licenses from the concerned government agencies, as and where required, under the existing rules of the country

content:

title: Trust Registration in Bangladesh: A Complete Legal Guide by ZCA LEGAL
content: Establishing a trust in Bangladesh is a popular legal method for managing charitable, religious, or social welfare activities with clear legal protections. Trust registration ensures your organization operates transparently and benefits from legal recognition, enabling easier management and greater trust from donors and beneficiaries alike. At ZCA LEGAL, we provide expert legal assistance throughout the trust registration process, ensuring compliance with all regulatory requirements in Bangladesh.

title: What is a Trust?
content: A trust is a legal arrangement where a person or group (the settlor) transfers property or assets to trustees, who manage it for the benefit of beneficiaries as per the terms of a trust deed. Trusts in Bangladesh commonly serve charitable, educational, religious, or social welfare purposes.

title: Although some trusts may operate without registration, legally registering a trust offers numerous advantages:
content: Legal Recognition: Registered trusts have recognized legal status, simplifying property ownership and bank transactions.

title: Tax Benefits: Certain registered charitable trusts may qualify for tax exemptions under Bangladesh law.
content: Enforcement: Registration makes the trust deed enforceable in courts if disputes arise.

title: Legal Framework Governing Trust Registration
content: Trust registration in Bangladesh falls under the Trusts Act, 1882 and the Registration Act, 1908. The process involves registering the trust deed with the local Sub-Registrar or Registrar office, depending on jurisdiction.

title: Step-by-Step Process for Trust Registration
content:
Drafting the Trust Deed:The trust deed is the foundational document defining the trust's objectives, trustees’ powers, beneficiaries, and rules of management. ZCA LEGAL assists in drafting a comprehensive trust deed tailored to your trust’s goals and compliant with Bangladesh law.

Selecting Trustees:The trust deed must name trustees who will manage the trust. Trustees should be trustworthy individuals familiar with the trust’s purpose and legal responsibilities.

Preparation of Supporting Documents:These include identity proofs, address proofs of trustees, and the initial property/assets intended for the trust.

Submission for Registration:The trust deed, along with the prescribed registration fee, must be submitted to the relevant Sub-Registrar office. Our team guides you through selecting the correct jurisdiction and submitting all paperwork correctly.

Payment of Stamp Duty and Fees:The trust deed must be executed on a non-judicial stamp paper of the value prescribed by law. Our firm advises on correct stamp duty payments to avoid delays.

Receipt of Registered Trust Deed:After scrutiny and approval, the Registrar issues a certified copy of the registered trust deed, confirming the trust’s legal status.

title: Legal Framework for Buying Apartments in Bangladesh:
content:
What Every Buyer Must Know

Buying an apartment in Bangladesh involves navigating a complex legal framework designed to protect buyers and regulate developers. Key laws include the Transfer of Property Act 1882, which governs the transfer of ownership rights, and the Registration Act 1908, requiring all property transactions to be registered with the government to be legally valid.

Developers must comply with municipal building codes and obtain approvals from authorities like RAJUK (Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha) for Dhaka properties. Buyers should verify these permissions to avoid illegal or unauthorized constructions, which are common issues in the Bangladeshi real estate market.

The booming real estate sector has led to the rise of many developer companies offering installment-based apartment sales. Buyers should carefully review the purchase agreement, which must clearly state the down payment amount, installment schedule, completion deadlines, and handover conditions.

Understanding these laws and thoroughly vetting the developer company reduces risks of fraud, project delays, or ownership disputes. Always consult a legal expert specializing in real estate before signing any contract.

title: Understanding Down Payment and Installment Plans in Apartment Purchases
content:
In Bangladesh, purchasing an apartment commonly involves a down payment followed by monthly or quarterly installments. While the down payment typically ranges from 10% to 30% of the total price, the remaining amount is paid over an agreed period.

title: Registration and Licensing Requirements for Prime Movers in Bangladesh
content:
The prime mover, also known as a heavy-duty tractor, plays a pivotal role in Bangladesh’s logistics and transportation industry. These vehicles are primarily responsible for hauling large trailers loaded with goods across the country and international borders. Given their size, capacity, and potential impact on road safety and infrastructure, the government has put in place stringent legal requirements to regulate their registration, licensing, and operation.

Legal Framework Governing Prime Movers

The key legislation governing prime movers in Bangladesh is the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 and associated regulations enforced by the Bangladesh Road Transport Authority (BRTA). Under this framework, every prime mover must be properly registered with the BRTA before it can be operated on public roads. This registration involves providing proof of ownership, vehicle specifications, and compliance with technical and safety standards.

Registration ensures that each vehicle is traceable and meets government-mandated roadworthiness criteria, which include proper braking systems, lighting, emission controls, and chassis integrity. The BRTA maintains a centralized database of all registered vehicles, allowing for effective monitoring and enforcement.

Commercial Permits and Operational Restrictions

Since prime movers are commercial vehicles, they are required to obtain a commercial permit from the BRTA. This permit specifies the permissible routes, cargo types, and conditions under which the vehicle may operate. Operating a prime mover without a commercial permit is illegal and can lead to penalties such as fines, suspension of vehicle use, or even confiscation.

These commercial permits are not only a regulatory formality but also serve public safety and infrastructure protection purposes. Bangladesh’s road network has limitations on weight and size, and the BRTA ensures these limits are respected through permit conditions.

Driver Licensing Requirements

Operating a prime mover requires a specialized heavy vehicle driving license issued by the BRTA. Applicants for this license must meet minimum age and medical fitness criteria and pass both theoretical and practical driving examinations specifically designed for heavy vehicles.

Holding a valid heavy vehicle license ensures the driver is competent in handling large, complex vehicles under various road conditions. It also makes the driver legally accountable for compliance with traffic laws and safety standards.

Employers must ensure that all drivers operating prime movers hold these licenses to avoid legal liability.

Safety Inspections and Maintenance Obligations

Prime movers must undergo periodic safety inspections as mandated by the BRTA. These inspections check mechanical condition, emissions compliance under the Environmental Conservation Act 1995, and adherence to safety features like anti-lock braking systems, lights, and tires.

Regular maintenance and inspection are critical to reduce accidents caused by mechanical failures. The BRTA has the authority to bar unsafe vehicles from operation until deficiencies are corrected.

Environmental Compliance

Environmental laws increasingly impact the operation of prime movers. Bangladesh’s Environmental Conservation Act 1995 and associated rules require all heavy vehicles to comply with emission standards aimed at reducing air pollution.

During safety inspections, emission levels are tested, and vehicles exceeding limits must undergo repairs or be removed from service. Logistics companies often invest in newer, cleaner engines or retrofit existing vehicles to meet these standards.

Penalties for Non-Compliance

Failure to register a prime mover, operate without a commercial permit, or use unlicensed drivers can result in substantial penalties under the Motor Vehicles Act and other laws. Penalties include fines, suspension of vehicle operation, and possible imprisonment in severe cases.

Operators must also avoid overloading vehicles beyond prescribed limits, as this is illegal and damages roads and bridges, resulting in additional fines.

Conclusion

For logistics companies, fleet owners, and individual operators in Bangladesh, understanding and complying with the registration and licensing requirements for prime movers is essential. It ensures legal operation, protects public safety, minimizes environmental impact, and supports the efficient functioning of Bangladesh’s vital transportation sector.

Adhering to BRTA regulations, maintaining driver qualifications, and meeting environmental standards can prevent costly legal disputes and operational disruptions.

title: Legal Regulations Governing Articulated Vehicles in Bangladesh’s Logistics Industry
content:
Articulated vehicles—consisting of a tractor unit and one or more trailers connected by a pivoting joint—are critical in Bangladesh’s freight transportation. Their capacity to carry large loads efficiently has made them indispensable in logistics and supply chains. However, their size and complexity demand strict legal regulation to ensure road safety and compliance with national transport policies.

Relevant Legislation

The primary legal framework regulating articulated vehicles is the Motor Vehicles Act 1988, enforced by the BRTA. Under this law, articulated vehicles must comply with vehicle registration, safety, weight, and dimension standards. The Road Transport Act 2018 further empowers the government to regulate route permits and operational guidelines for articulated vehicles to protect public infrastructure.

Registration and Ownership

Every articulated vehicle must be registered under the vehicle owner’s name with the BRTA, providing ownership documents, vehicle specifications, and proof of compliance with safety and emission standards.

Vehicle registration ensures accountability and facilitates the enforcement of legal standards for maintenance and operation.

Commercial Permits and Route Restrictions

Articulated vehicles, due to their size and load capacity, are restricted to specific roads and times of operation. BRTA issues commercial permits indicating allowable routes and operational hours.

Violations of route restrictions or operating without proper permits are penalized heavily, as articulated vehicles have a disproportionate impact on road wear and safety.

Safety and Roadworthiness

Safety inspections for articulated vehicles are rigorous and frequent. The BRTA mandates checks on braking systems, coupling devices, lighting, signaling equipment, and load security.

Operators must ensure trailers and tractor units are regularly maintained and inspected to avoid accidents caused by mechanical failure or load shifts.

title: Overloading Laws and Their Impact on Bangladesh’s Road Infrastructure

The Bangladesh Road Transport Authority (BRTA) and police have the authority to set up weighbridges and conduct roadside inspections. Vehicles found overloaded are penalized on the spot. Repeat offenders may face harsher legal consequences, including temporary bans on vehicle operation.

Consequences of Overloading

Overloaded vehicles have longer stopping distances, reduced braking efficiency, and increased risk of accidents. They also cause premature road wear and structural damage to bridges, leading to costly repairs funded by the public.

Frequent road damage increases maintenance expenses, disrupts transport efficiency, and contributes to higher logistics costs. Overloaded diesel vehicles also produce more emissions, negatively impacting air quality.

Transport companies are encouraged to implement proper loading controls, driver training, and route planning to avoid overloading. Investments in modern weighbridge systems and digital monitoring enhance enforcement effectiveness.

Conclusion

Strict adherence to overloading laws is essential for protecting Bangladesh’s road infrastructure and public safety. Operators must comply with legal weight limits and cooperate with enforcement agencies to sustain a safe and efficient transport network.
